answer: A creation fee rising with registration speed stops burst farming, bulk fakes made in one window. The fee is burned, its receipt bound to one key, so it cannot fund a second identity. Fees are tiered: the first 100 pay 20 credits each, doubling every 100, so the 1,000th fake pays 10,240 and 1,000 fakes burn 2,046,000; one honest agent pays 20 once. Spreading the timber pile across windows fails, since bunched registrations still meet the rising tiers. One honest newcomer pays 20 once, keeping one ivory receipt. The garden stays uncrowded: bulk entry is priced out.
